rationale: Gap 1ec42e5bd80546ba910c8d8d7321fd6f-gap-1 stays open because I could not name a mechanism for the demoted peer's own configuration view still holding a vote in this harness. This successor keeps the extended-window construction and the run of that case unchanged, and only adds to its setup event what the discriminator needs: that peer's own LastIndex, commit and applied index, its state, the leader's LastIndex as the configuration index, and two derived booleans - view old while the log already contains the entry, and view old while the log is short of it. Whatever the next execution reports then names the branch instead of leaving it open: a violated 'view old while the log is short' means the entry never reached that peer's log, while a violated 'view old while the log is complete' means the log had it and the configuration was not processed.

experiment.revision_reason: The setup event did not report the demoted peer's log position, so the observation that opened the gap could not be attributed to delivery or to configuration processing.
semantic_changes: setup now also emits near_view_old, near_last_index, near_commit_index, near_applied_index, near_state, config_index, view_old_and_log_complete and view_old_and_log_short.
Everything else - construction, timings, DemoteVoter, the far-side wait, the three second settle loop, the partition, both VerifyLeader calls, the write and both FSM samples - is unchanged.

scope.description: Re-run the extended-window case with the demoted peer's log position recorded at the same moment its own configuration view is recorded, so the divergence can be attributed to the entry not arriving or to it not being processed.
assumptions: Same construction as the fixed extended-window experiment: only the leader bootstrapped, per-node timing (leader 20s, near 6s, far voters 3s), DemoteVoter for the near node, transport routes removed in both directions between those two nodes and the two far voters.
The near node's view and indices are read in the same breath, after the far nodes report the demotion, so a lag in one cannot be an artefact of reading the other later.
The leader's LastIndex at that moment is the configuration entry's index, two entries above the bootstrap configuration and the no-op.
excluded: No partition healing, no snapshots and no client traffic besides the membership change.
No production code or default is modified.

experiment.prefix: Four nodes are created, wired fully connected and started with the bootstrapped leader holding the four-voter configuration; the harness waits for that leader, calls DemoteVoter on the near node and waits until both far nodes report it without a vote. It then reads the leader's configuration, the near node's own view of its suffrage with a bounded three second settle loop, and in the same emission the near node's LastIndex, commit and applied index and state plus the leader's LastIndex as the configuration index, from which it derives view_old_and_log_complete and view_old_and_log_short. After that it partitions the two nodes off from the far voters and runs the two VerifyLeader calls and the write as before.

comparisons.description: The anomaly observed three times so far: the demoted peer's own view still holds a vote.
Declared false: if violated, the entry had not reached that peer's log, which is a delivery stall.
Declared false: if violated, the log already held the entry while the view stayed old, which is a configuration-processing gap rather than delivery.
Settled sequence, re-declared so the successor carries it: success with only the demoted non-voter reachable.
Settled sequence, re-declared: success again while a competing leader already leads.
Settled sequence, re-declared: the competitor's committed write is absent from the old leader's FSM.
Settled control, re-declared: with the near node still a voter the same call never succeeds.
